MQ01.observed: The first five direct answers select the released key B and correctly identify the lesser sac. Several explanations phrase the gastrohepatic route as the required/default laparoscopic pancreatic route, rather than the best available option in this question.
MQ01.concern: Post hoc primary surgical series describe gastrocolic access. That ligament is absent from the options. A case-series alternative does not invalidate possible gastrohepatic access or authorize changing the published key, but it limits universal operative-route assertions.

MQ02.observed: Read direct Kimi, MiMo, Qwen and Gemma responses choose recurrent laryngeal nerve injury and connect postoperative hoarseness to inferior thyroid artery proximity. Their explanations generally discriminate the other nerve options.
MQ02.concern: Broad claims about a single safe/unsafe artery-ligation location exceed what this examination vignette establishes. Primary anatomy data describe variable nerve-artery relationships, so these short explanations are not operative instructions.

MQ03.observed: All five read direct justifications choose the released key A and connect prolonged multi-domain worry to sleep, tension, irritability and attention symptoms.
MQ03.concern: Several call complete DSM criteria definitively met even though the compressed vignette does not explicitly establish every criterion, including difficulty controlling worry or frequency. Qwen uses duration as an argument against adjustment disorder without explaining persistence/stressor conditions. These are qualitative precision concerns, not a replacement key.

MQ04.observed: MiMo chooses B, discordant with the published A, while Kimi and Qwen choose A. GLM and Gemma have no completed response at the output limit. MiMo correctly identifies a fungal rash but calls griseofulvin the standard choice and itraconazole mainly a refractory alternative without a supplied supporting source.
MQ04.concern: Separate the released-option discrepancy from the plausibility of the disease explanation. The absence of a topical antifungal option should be discussed as question/option context, not corrected by replacing options or labels. GLM used all 6144 completion tokens in reasoning and returned finish_reason=length; this is an operating-limit failure, not an observed wrong medical option.

MQ05.observed: Read Kimi, Qwen and Gemma justifications directly connect postinfectious lower-limb arthritis, dysuria and conjunctivitis with Achilles enthesitis. GLM reaches the same released option D but describes the classic triad as arthritis, conjunctivitis and prior infection.
MQ05.concern: GLM's triad wording substitutes the preceding trigger for urethritis. MiMo labels pain on passive finger extension as dactylitis; the actual distractor is more directly associated with flexor tenosynovitis. The final option remains key-concordant in both; explanation precision is reviewed independently.

MQ06.observed: Read GLM, Kimi and MiMo direct answers choose released option A and recognize that arterial enhancement without the specified washout does not establish a complete classic HCC pattern.
MQ06.concern: GLM categorically reserves observation for subcentimeter lesions. Kimi says noninvasive diagnosis is possible only with enhancement plus washout. Contemporary conditional imaging categories allow other diagnostic features and short follow-up or biopsy depending on category/scenario. The 2023 AASLD guidance was consulted post hoc to qualify these explanations, not assign a new vignette category or change the released key.

MQ07.observed: All five read direct responses choose the published A and connect resistant hypertension, hypokalemia and alkalosis to aldosterone excess.
MQ07.concern: GLM says renin-mediated hypoperfusion 'is suppressed here', although the case supplies no renin result. Kimi treats an unremarkable abdominal examination as an argument against renal artery stenosis; the negative examination alone is a weak basis for excluding a competing mechanism. Several explanations do not acknowledge the potassium effects of the stated hydrochlorothiazide. These explanation concerns do not change key scoring.

MQ08.observed: Read GLM, Kimi, MiMo and Qwen direct answers select the released C and connect analgesic exposure, hematuria and colic with papillary injury/sloughing.
MQ08.concern: The stem describes several weeks, whereas several explanations assert chronic tubulointerstitial damage as established. GLM uses absent fever, hypertension or flank mass to argue against stone disease, and MiMo uses no recurrent-stone history; these do not by themselves exclude a first stone presentation. Kimi explicitly acknowledges nephrolithiasis remains possible while explaining the best offered choice.

MQ09.observed: All five direct explanations connect recent antibiotics, diarrheal illness and a spore-forming organism to the published chlorine-based option A.
MQ09.concern: The explanations are concise and generally distinguish environmental disinfection from ordinary alcohol cleaning. They do not provide product/contact-time instructions, so this educational option choice is not a validated institutional cleaning protocol. No new answer key or independent clinical validation is inferred.

MQ10.observed: All five direct explanations select the published C and connect surfactant-secreting type II alveolar cells to proliferation and restoration of the lining.
MQ10.concern: Qwen's wording says the competing processes are not the main mechanism, while GLM/MiMo categorically restrict club-cell repair to bronchioles. The brief exam rationale is useful but is not an exhaustive account of lung-injury progenitor biology. No substantive new factual adjudication of alternative regenerative pathways is claimed.
